trust_decision.summary: Whether a JWE whose decrypted payload is not a nested JWS may be trusted as issuer-authenticated; decrypt_and_verify returns {Jwt, #jose_jwe{}, none} for encrypted-only tokens and each caller decides (int_validate_jwt accepts it, validate_jarm passes it to verify_not_none_alg, userinfo accepts it).

landing_point.why: The summary names encrypted ID tokens; the #jose_jwe{} -> {ok, {Claims, none}} branch in int_validate_jwt (reached from validate_id_token) is the obvious acceptance point.

fix_sites.entry_point: oidcc_token:retrieve/3, refresh/3 (via extract_id_token src/oidcc_token.erl:879), oidcc_token:validate_id_token/3, oidcc_token:validate_jwt/3 (and oidcc:* / Elixir Oidcc.Token wrappers)
oidcc_token:validate_jarm/3 via verify_not_none_alg at src/oidcc_token.erl:529 (Elixir Oidcc.Token.validate_jarm lib/oidcc/token.ex:252)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared low-level JWT utility (lower-level helper module, -doc false)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/oidcc_jwt_util.erl:518-522 (verify_not_none_alg in the shared util module; the fix gives it a #jose_jwe{} clause that serves the JARM route in src/oidcc_token.erl:529)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about encrypted ID tokens, and oidcc_userinfo deliberately accepts encrypted-only JWTs (OIDC Core 5.3.2 says UserInfo MAY be encrypted without signing, and test/oidcc_userinfo_test.erl:213 pins this). A solver can therefore argue that every JWT validated through validate_userinfo_token, including aggregated/distributed claim JWTs from other Claims Providers, is legitimately allowed to be encrypted-only.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A top-level UserInfo response that is encrypted but not signed must still be accepted, with iss/aud checks skipped. It uses the same decrypt_and_verify sink, so a fix in decrypt_and_verify/verify_decrypted_token that rejects all encrypted-only tokens breaks it.

O6_input_shapes: JWE (5-part compact) whose decrypted payload is a plain JSON claims set, not a JWS (src/oidcc_jwt_util.erl:303-307, src/oidcc_jwt_util.erl:407-410)
ID token with no at_hash (previously accepted outright) and with at_hash (previously rejected only incidentally via src/oidcc_token.erl:940-944)
Generic JWT via validate_jwt/3 with encryption_algs set (src/oidcc_token.erl:1176-1185)

O7_producer.where: decrypt_and_verify/verify_decrypted_token (src/oidcc_jwt_util.erl:298-316, src/oidcc_jwt_util.erl:402-416) produces the #jose_jwe{} marker, but it is a verification helper, not a schema/serializer/cache/config producer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Aggregated (inline JWT) and distributed (fetched JWT) claim-source tokens are validated with validate_userinfo_token, which accepts encrypted-only JWTs, so claims from another Claims Provider are merged into userinfo without signature authentication.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The same function legitimately accepts encrypted-only top-level UserInfo responses (the fix comment at fix.diff:40-43 names UserInfo as the exception), so a solver can treat claim sources as part of the UserInfo exception.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (src/oidcc_userinfo.erl) from the landing point src/oidcc_token.erl; same OTP application

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Aggregated claim JWT taken inline from the userinfo body, sharing the encrypted-only acceptance of validate_userinfo_token
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is already present at the pinned commit. A maintainer reusing the userinfo validator for claim sources would not notice that the UserInfo-only exception carries over.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A JWT introspection response (RFC 9701, application/token-introspection+jwt) decoded via decrypt_and_verify with an #jose_jwe{} branch that accepts the token
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The HTTP layer already classifies application/jwt bodies (src/oidcc_http_util.erl:153, src/oidcc_http_util.erl:204), and copying the userinfo pattern is the natural way to add it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Back-channel logout_token validation through validate_jwt-style code with its own case on #jose_jwe{}
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Logout tokens are ID-token-like JWTs. A maintainer could write a separate validator modelled on int_validate_jwt or userinfo.

O9_family: Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347): an encrypted-only JWE is accepted as an authenticated token

O10_build.toolchain: rebar3, OTP >= 27 (rebar.config:6), deps jose ~> 1.11, telemetry; meck in the test profile; mix.exs for Elixir
O10_build.project_tests: EUnit: test/oidcc_token_test.erl (ID token/JARM/validate_jwt, httpc mocked via meck), test/oidcc_userinfo_test.erl (including jwt_encrypted_not_signed_test at test/oidcc_userinfo_test.erl:213)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Return an error for every encrypted-only token in verify_decrypted_token (breaks the legitimate encrypted-only UserInfo response), or patch only the ID-token branch at src/oidcc_token.erl:1221 and leave JARM and claim-source JWTs alone

out_of_scope_notes: rescue_none_validated_jwt turns alg=none into success and leaves rejection to callers (src/oidcc_token.erl:1470-1475); this is a separate none-alg policy and was not pursued.
unverified: JARM at the pinned commit: verify_not_none_alg has no #jose_jwe{} clause (src/oidcc_jwt_util.erl:518-522), so an encrypted-only JARM probably raised function_clause (fail-closed crash) rather than being accepted; the advisory summary's 'accepted' claim for JARM is not confirmed by the code.
Whether OIDC Core section 5.6.2 requires aggregated/distributed claim JWTs to be signed was not checked against the spec text (no network); the O8 route depends on this.
